notes: Identity assessment: supplied canonical text is a complete six-page primary experimental report, with title ARE WE ALL LESS RISKY AND MORE SKILLFUL THAN OUR FELLOW DRIVERS?, author Ola SVENSON, and Acta Psychologica 47 (1981) 143-148, matching the neutral original reference. DOI is not printed in the supplied text, so DOI identity was not independently confirmed; bibliographic identity and document type match. No PDF was supplied. Both assigned rows have the same safety description and original p. 3 locator (printed p. 145, Table 1). Table 1 distinguishes US and Swedish safety samples, and neither locator identifies a country. No target was assigned by row order or numeric correspondence. Candidate participant Ns: US safety 40; Swedish safety 35 (Subjects, p. 144). These are separately reported country-specific judgment samples, with no exclusions stated; no pooled critical test is reported, so no N sum is extracted. Candidate descriptive results: 88% (US) and 77% (Swedish) believed themselves safer than the median driver (Results, p. 146). Table 1 gives percentile-category distributions; these percentages are descriptive proportions, not a named standardized effect size. No effect-size conversion performed. Results and Table 1 report distributions, median intervals and percentages, without inferential test statistics or p values. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders.
